title: Zadar Prices and Realistic 2027 Budget Guide
metaDescription: Zadar costs €50–70 a day on a budget, €90–140 mid-range and €250+ for luxury. See 2027 price estimates for hotels, food, transport and day trips.
content:
## How Much Does Zadar Cost in 2027?

Zadar remains cheaper than Dubrovnik, Split and Hvar, but it is no longer a bargain. Recent price trackers put a budget day at €50–70, a mid-range day at €80–140 and a luxury day at €250 or more per person. Those figures exclude flights.

The 2027 numbers below add a cautious 3–6% to 2026 prices. That is an estimate, based on how Croatian hospitality prices have moved since euro adoption in 2023. Actual rates for 2027 will be published by hotels and apartment hosts in late 2026 and early 2027.

### Daily Budget by Travel Style (2027 Estimate, Per Person)

| Style | Daily budget | 7-day total (excl. flights) |
|---|---|---|
| Budget (hostel or room, self-catering, walking) | €55–80 | €385–560 |
| Mid-range (apartment or 3–4 star, restaurants, one boat trip) | €90–140 | €630–980 |
| Luxury (4–5 star, fine dining, private tours) | €250+ | €1,750+ |

Solo travelers pay more per person because a double room costs nearly the same as a single. A solo traveler using hostels typically spends €75–110 a day in summer. Couples sharing an apartment usually come in lower per person.

## How Have Zadar Prices Changed Recently?

Three shifts stand out:

- **Accommodation has risen the most.** Average hotel rates across booking platforms in 2026 sit around €100–120 for a mid-range room, with peak summer rates reaching €160–230. Hostel dorm beds now commonly cost €25–45 in season, up from roughly €15–25 a few years ago.
- **Restaurant prices rose after euro adoption.** A three-course dinner for two at a mid-range restaurant is now about €65. Coffee and cocktails in the Old Town cost noticeably more than in neighborhoods away from the center.
- **Transport and attractions rose modestly.** Local bus tickets are around €1.50, and the airport bus is about €5. Day tours to national parks have moved to the €40–90 range.

Seasonality still matters more than inflation. Mid-range hotel rates roughly double between winter (about €50–70) and the July–August peak (about €100–165). A week in late April costs far less than the same week in August.

## Accommodation Costs in Zadar

### Hostels

Zadar has more than 20 hostels. Dorm beds average €25–45 per night in season, with the cheapest beds around €15–20 in winter. Sky Hostel and Hostel Sunset are two established options with strong guest ratings (9.2 and 8.5 out of 10 respectively on a major booking platform).

### Apartments and Private Rooms

Private apartments run about €70–150 per night in high season. Private rooms in family-run houses cost less, often €45–80. Apartments with a kitchen cut food costs by €15–25 per person per day.

### Hotels

- **3-star:** €70–100 in spring and autumn, €100–165 in summer.
- **4-star:** about €107–120 on average, higher in July and August.
- **5-star and resort-style:** The Hyatt Regency Zadar averages around €157–164 for a double. Peak-summer luxury rates reach €200–300.

For 2027, expect each category to land 3–6% above these figures, with summer weekends increasing the most.

## Food and Drink Prices in Zadar

| Item | Typical price |
|---|---|
| Budget day of food (bakery, market, simple lunch) | €20–25 |
| Mid-range day of food | €45–50 |
| Three-course dinner for two | ~€65 |
| Coffee | €2–3 |
| Local beer (0.3–0.5 l) | €3.50–5 |

Budget travelers eat well on burek from a bakery, fruit and fish from the Old Town market, and a set lunch (marenda or daily menu) at a local konoba. Dalmatian dishes worth ordering include black risotto, grilled fish by weight, pasticada and octopus peka, which usually needs to be ordered a few hours ahead. Maraschino cherry liqueur, produced in Zadar, is the local drink to try.

## Getting Around: Transport Costs

- **Airport to city:** Zadar Airport is about 12 km east of the center. The bus costs about €5 and takes 20–30 minutes. A taxi or ride-hailing trip costs roughly €20–30.
- **City buses:** about €1.50 per ticket.
- **Taxi or Bolt in town:** €5–10 for a short ride.
- **Rental car:** €30–60 per day, with high-season rates at the upper end.
- **Old Town:** fully walkable. The peninsula is under 3 km long.

A car is only worth renting for Paklenica, Nin salt flats or Krka. For Kornati and Plitvice, organized tours are simpler and cost about the same once fuel, parking and entry are counted.

## Activities and Day Trip Prices

- **Old Town sights:** The Sea Organ and Greeting to the Sun are free and best at sunset. Church and museum entries are typically a few euros each.
- **Kornati National Park boat tour:** €40–70 per person for a full day, often with lunch. Park entry may be extra.
- **Krka National Park tour:** €40–60 plus the park entrance fee, which is higher in summer than in winter.
- **Plitvice Lakes tour:** €70–90 for a full day, with 1.5–2 hours each way.
- **Island ferry to Ugljan or Pašman:** a few euros each way from the Zadar passenger port, making it the cheapest way to get a beach day.

## Best Time to Visit Zadar for Lower Prices

Accommodation costs peak in July and August. The cheapest months are November to March, when prices run 30–50% below summer. April, May, late September and October offer the best balance: warm enough for the sea in September, and hotels about 30–40% under peak.

Booking at least 50 days ahead lowers hotel prices according to booking platform data. For 2027, reserving summer apartments between January and March is the safer plan, since the best-located places in the Old Town and Borik sell out first.

## Sample 2027 Budgets

### One Week, Budget Traveler (Shoulder Season)

Room or hostel €35–55 per night, groceries and one simple meal out €20 per day, transport €2–5 per day, one Krka or Kornati trip €50. Total: about €500–650.

### One Week, Couple, Mid-Range (June or September)

Apartment €90–120 per night, food and drinks €90 per day for two, transport and activities €30 per day, two day trips €160. Total for two: about €1,500–1,900, or €750–950 per person.

### One Week, Luxury (July)

Hotel €250–350 per night, fine dining €100–150 per person per day, private boat or car transfers. Total: €2,500–3,500 per person.

## Money-Saving Tips for Zadar

- **Stay outside the peninsula.** Apartments in Arbanasi, Bili Brig or Diklo cost less than the Old Town and are 10–20 minutes on foot or by bus.
- **Eat the lunch menu.** Many konobas away from the Kalelarga main street offer a set lunch that costs less than an evening à la carte meal.
- **Buy at the market.** The produce market near the Old Town wall sells cheese, figs, olive oil and fish at lower prices than shops on the main street.
- **Book tours directly.** Boat operators at the harbor often match or beat online prices for Kornati trips.
- **Skip the July–August weekend.** Even moving a trip by one week into late June or early September can cut accommodation by 20–30%.

The most useful single decision for a Zadar budget is the travel month. A September trip delivers summer weather at close to spring prices, and is the better value than August in nearly every case.

## Is Zadar Cheaper Than Dubrovnik or Split?

Yes. A mid-range day in Zadar costs roughly €90–140, while a similar day in Dubrovnik often exceeds €220. Zadar's Old Town is also less crowded with cruise-ship traffic, which keeps café and restaurant prices lower.

faq.question: How much money do I need per day in Zadar in 2027?
faq.answer: Plan on €55–80 per day on a budget, €90–140 for mid-range and €250 or more for luxury, per person and excluding flights. These estimates add about 3–6% to 2026 prices. Costs are highest in July and August.

faq.question: Is Zadar expensive compared with other Croatian cities?
faq.answer: Zadar is cheaper than Dubrovnik and generally below Split. Mid-range days cost about €90–140 in Zadar versus €220 or more in Dubrovnik. Summer hotel prices are still high, so shoulder-season travel gives the best value.

faq.question: What is the cheapest time to visit Zadar?
faq.answer: November to March is cheapest, with prices 30–50% below peak. April, May and October give lower rates with workable weather. July and August are the most expensive months.

faq.question: How much does a hotel in Zadar cost per night?
faq.answer: A 3-star hotel costs about €70–100 in spring and autumn and €100–165 in summer. Four-star hotels average roughly €107–120, and resort-style options such as the Hyatt Regency Zadar are around €157–164 for a double. Hostel dorm beds start around €25 in season.

faq.question: How do I get from Zadar Airport to the city?
faq.answer: The airport is about 12 km from the center. The airport bus costs about €5 and takes 20–30 minutes, while a taxi or ride-hailing trip costs roughly €20–30.

faq.question: How much do day trips from Zadar cost?
faq.answer: Kornati boat tours cost €40–70, Krka tours €40–60 plus entrance, and Plitvice Lakes tours €70–90. Prices usually include transport, and Kornati tours often include lunch.

faq.question: How many days are enough for Zadar?
faq.answer: Three days cover the Old Town, the Sea Organ and one island or park trip. Add two more days for Krka, Kornati or Paklenica. A longer stay lowers the average nightly cost if an apartment is booked weekly.

quickAnswer: A realistic 2027 Zadar budget is €55–80 per person per day for budget travel, €90–140 for mid-range and €250+ for luxury, based on 2026 prices plus an expected 3–6% rise. July and August push hotel rates up by roughly 50–100% over winter and spring.
